project.name: Larkfield breach response
project.brief: This one isn't an OOP project. It's the kind of thing OOP writes newsletters about. On Sept 25, Larkfield Benefits, a dental insurance company with 400,000 members, found out that one of its vendors had left a server open to the internet with member names, addresses, and member ID numbers on it. Federal law gives Larkfield 60 days from discovery to notify every affected member and the federal government, which makes the deadline Nov 24, and it is not moving. The project tracker says things are mostly on track. Your job is to figure out what's really going on before the deadline
project.company: Larkfield Benefits, a dental insurance company with 400,000 members

notes.title: Incident response sync
bullets: Dale opened by reading the trust restoration roadmap. It has four pillars
Member letter, data scope, and vendor logs: Rhys is waiting on Victor, Victor is waiting on Monique, Monique's vendor is waiting on Rhys's letter. Abe suggested "a call"
Ingrid owns the risk assessment, every regulator notice, and sign-off on every word members see. She joined 20 minutes late from another call
Forensics: Victor says on track. Carmen asked what "scope revision pending" means. Victor said "more people." Moved on
Credit monitoring: 90% done. The last 10% is that the contract covers 100,000 people and we're notifying 400,000
Call center script: 90% done. It says no financial information was involved
Mailing: the ticket says TBD until we know the scope. The print vendor needed a booking by Oct 9 to mail 400,000 letters in time
Extra phone staff for when the letters land: nobody owns it
Removing the vendor's access is still assigned to Stuart, who left in August. Nobody has checked whether it happened
Two press statements are being written, Rhys's and Dale's. Agreed Dale's "has more heart"
The deadline stays Nov 24, 60 days from discovery
